assumptions: The assessment unit is one benefit offered to one client; separate benefits in a package require separate assessment.
Both alternatives use the circular’s defined distributor population as a common bounded scope.
A product-type linkage is substantive; its existence requires assessment of the offer’s terms and presentation.
The discount exception continues to apply to gifts mentioned in the final sentence.
Unknown classification or connection facts remain unknown.

citations.quote: distributors should not offer any gifts (other than a discount of fees or charges) in promoting a specific investment product or a particular type of investment product to a client.

If gifts are offered in such a way that they are linked to a particular type of investment product, such as certain types of funds or funds offered by certain fund houses, then such gifts will be bound by this requirement
as they may be considered a gift that should not be offered to investors.

node.0a42d96ace6364d9d25890f9.distinction: Product-type linkage is sufficient to bring an otherwise qualifying gift offer within the control, even without a separately established promotional finding. This gives operative force to the final sentence’s if/then formulation. The strongest uncertainty is what linkage must comprise; the missing FAQ may make promotional connection intrinsic to that concept.

node.0a42d96ace6364d9d25890f9.statement: [TRUE_IS_PROHIBITED] For the selected paragraph-10 gift-promotion control, within the stated actor-and-offer scope, true means the assessed benefit is a gift, is not a fees-or-charges discount, and either has the specified promotional connection or is offered in a manner linking it to a particular investment-product type. Actual investor distraction need not be proved. This is a proposed reading of the selected control only.
node.0a42d96ace6364d9d25890f9.subject: Paragraph-10 gift control: product-type linkage as a sufficient connection

assumptions: Assess one identified benefit offered in one identified promotion; a mixed package requires separate classification of its components.
The proposal is limited to SFC-authorised-fund distribution and assumes temporal applicability has been established separately.
Gift status, discount status and promotional linkage remain supplied judgments; no unknown fact is assigned a truth value.
The packet supports one definite core reading. The treatment of rebates and indirect promotional links remains unresolved rather than being converted into unsupported competing rules.

citations.quote: as they may be considered a gift that should not be offered to investors.

Paragraph 3.11 of the Code of Conduct provides that distributors should not offer any gifts (other than a discount of fees or charges) in promoting a specific investment product or a particular type of investment product to a client.

If gifts are offered in such a way that they are linked to a particular type of investment product, such as certain types of funds or funds offered by certain fund houses, then such gifts will be bound by this requirement
in breach of section 103 of the SFO or paragraph 3.11 of the Code of Conduct.
3 The answer to question 1 of the frequently asked questions on the Code of Conduct issued by the SFC on 30 September 2010.

node.2d30e4cecd6d9334b7831eec.distinction: The selected control turns on a non-exempt gift offered in a product-linked promotion. It is not an unconditional ban on every additional return, and it does not require either structured-product status or proof of actual distraction. Its strongest unresolved boundary is whether a particular monetary benefit genuinely constitutes a fee or charge discount; the supplied text does not settle rebate mechanics.

node.2d30e4cecd6d9334b7831eec.statement: [TRUE_IS_PROHIBITED] For the selected paragraph-10 gift-promotion control, within the stated scope, true means the offered benefit is a gift falling outside the fee-or-charge discount exception and thus falls within the stated 'should not offer' requirement. False means only that this selected gift condition is not met; an out-of-scope offer is not assessed. Neither outcome establishes overall compliance or resolves section 103.
